note: dw-check and dw-land both render a verdict over a diff. The whole distinction is timing — mid-build and repeatable versus once at the end, promoting residue — so the negatives put that boundary under load rather than picking distant skills. The outside-reviewer positive is here because delegation is now what bare does, so asking for one is a first-class way in and not a synonym for typing /codex:review.

positives.prompt: give what I have written so far a once-over before I carry on
positives.note: Scores zero everywhere, and counted in the blank column. The only terms carrying signal are "written" and "far", and "far" belongs to dw-handoff. A real vocabulary gap: dw-check's description has no words for a mid-build once-over. Widening it is its own measurement.

positives.prompt: anything wrong with the code I just wrote? point me at the lines
quick pass over my diff for correctness and whether it matches how this repo does things
sanity-check the work in progress, I am halfway through and want a second opinion
get an outside reviewer onto the change I am building

negatives.prompt: this change is done — final verdict, then file whatever is worth keeping
negatives.note: The timing boundary. Anything mentioning finishing or promoting belongs to dw-land.

negatives.prompt: this change is finished — give the verdict, promote what is worth keeping and open its PR
negatives.note: Replaced a plain-git negative when dw-git left the corpus: a bare commit-and-push now routes to no skill at all, which the eval reads as blank, so the near-miss is the closing verdict that also reads a diff.
